title: Saying a, an, and no article
goal: Choose en, ei, et, or no article in simple singular noun phrases.

objectives.statement: Choose en, ei, et, or no article in simple singular noun phrases.

spans.value: Amina has recently moved to Bergen to study. She is looking at a room in a shared flat. Lars, who already lives there, shows her around.
Ja, det stemmer. Jeg ser etter et rom.

blocks.translation: Yes, that’s right. I’m looking for a room.

spans.value: Her er rommet. Det har en seng, ei hylle og et skrivebord.

blocks.translation: Here is the room. It has a bed, a shelf, and a desk.

spans.value: Det ser fint ut. Er det et kjøkken også?

blocks.translation: It looks nice. Is there a kitchen too?

spans.value: Ja. Vil du ha kaffe eller te?

blocks.translation: Yes. Would you like coffee or tea?

spans.value: Kaffe, takk. Er det andre studenter som bor her?

blocks.translation: Coffee, please. Are there other students living here?

spans.value: Nei, men Ingrid bor i rommet ved siden av. Hun er lærer. Jeg er student.

blocks.translation: No, but Ingrid lives in the room next door. She is a teacher. I’m a student.

spans.value: Da passer det bra. Jeg er student også.

blocks.translation: Then it suits me well. I’m a student too.

sections.title: Choosing the article in a sentence

spans.value: The article remains directly before the noun in a simple noun phrase:
A common mistake is to omit the article because the listener understands which kind of object is meant:
For one ordinary countable object, this is incomplete. Say:
Another mistake is to choose an article according to the person connected with the noun. Grammatical gender does not change according to a person’s sex:

spans.value: refer to drinks as substances. Lars is not counting individual cups, so there is no article.
These nouns can sometimes be used with an article when the speaker means one countable serving or item. Compare:
The first sentence can mean that she buys coffee as a product, perhaps a bag of coffee for the flat. The second means one serving, usually one cup of coffee.
The same contrast appears in a café:

no.value: Jeg vil gjerne ha en te.

spans.value: The version without an article focuses on the drink. The version with
treats the order as one serving.
Do not assume that every food or drink noun must always lack an article. Ask what the speaker means: a substance in general, or one countable serving or item?

prompt.value: Choose the message that fits the information. Use «ei» before the feminine noun here; in Bokmål, «en» is also accepted before many feminine nouns.

explanation.value: Bruk «en kopp», «ei bok» og «et kart» om de tre tingene. Et yrke etter «er» står uten artikkel, og «te» som drikke står også uten artikkel.

options.text: I sekken har jeg ei kopp, ei bok og et kart. Romkameraten min er lege. Vi drikker te hjemme.
options.why: Kopp is masculine in the lesson’s convention and takes en.

options.text: I sekken har jeg en kopp, ei bok og et kart. Romkameraten min er en lege. Vi drikker te hjemme.
options.why: In this neutral description, lege names a role after er and is normally bare.

options.text: I sekken har jeg en kopp, ei bok og et kart. Romkameraten min er lege. Vi drikker en te hjemme.
options.why: The stem means tea as a beverage; en te would mean one serving.

prompt.value: Nora asks about your new shared flat. Reply to Nora. Say who you live with, what the room and kitchen are like, that your flatmate works as a cook, and that you drink coffee at home. Use «en», «ei», and «et» before singular count nouns; use «ei» here.

Criteria whose ids end in -observation are diagnostic and must never make the response fail. Report a verdict for every criterion id.

criteria.instruction: The response is a message to Nora describing the new shared flat.

The response mentions a neighbor, a lamp in the room, and a shared kitchen; says the flatmate is a cook; and says coffee is drunk at home, either as a beverage without an article or as one serving with «en kaffe».

The response uses en with a masculine countable noun, ei with a feminine countable noun, and et with a neuter countable noun, following the requested lesson pattern. Treat accepted en forms for feminine nouns as linguistically valid, though the prompt asks for ei here to demonstrate the pattern.

The neighbor and lamp are expressed with suitable articles if phrased as singular countable nouns. The shared kitchen may naturally be expressed with bare «kjøkken» after «dele» or as «et kjøkken». The flatmate's role as cook is expressed without an indefinite article. Coffee may be expressed as the beverage without an article or as one serving with «en kaffe». Accept natural rephrasing that preserves those meanings.
The Norwegian is comprehensible enough for Nora to understand the description.
